selection_rationale: Three independent public-source collections are immediately schedulable and need no local profile, driver, process, GPU, build, or test result: relational-query fusion boundaries, tile-renderer attachment lifetime, and single-GPU BFS direction/frontier representation. They exclude current Strata measurement questions and each other.

scopes.title: Fusion and materialization boundaries in GPU analytical query pipelines
scopes.finite_question: For single-GPU analytical queries over columnar relations, compare operator-at-a-time kernels that materialize each result, a fully fused selection/filter/projection-to-aggregate pipeline, and relaxed or staged fusion with materialization at selected pipeline breakers. How do selectivity, projected width, intermediate reuse/fan-out, launch cost, live state/register pressure, and parallelism move the boundary? Keep hash-join and aggregate internals as examples of boundaries, not separate algorithm surveys.
scopes.breadth_and_counterevidence: Use original GPU database papers and a few query-engine/compiler papers. Compare all three execution styles in one table; separate published timings from byte/launch models. Record GPU, query/workload, layout, cardinality/selectivity, fusion unit, compile/setup treatment, and timing boundary. Do not compare headline speedups from unlike experiments. Include cases where fusion removes large intermediates/launches and counterexamples where full fusion loses through register/resource pressure, low occupancy, compile cost, fan-out/reuse, pipeline breakers, or reduced parallelism. Treat selection/compaction costs explicitly. No Arc/Strata claim.
scopes.novelty_guard: No indexed/reviewed report covers relational query pipeline materialization/fusion. R759/R763 are general GPU work partition/residency; R786 is graph fan-in/reduction; R855 is convolution mapping; R829 is tensor compression. Limit this to relational selection/projection/lightweight aggregation and pipeline boundaries. Exclude convolution, generic tensor fusion, IO/decompression fusion, hash-join algorithm design, graph aggregation internals, CUDA Graph/replay, and product changes.
scopes.report_budget: 1,300–1,700 substantive words; no more than 7 primary URLs; one three-strategy table, a bounded byte/launch model, at least one win and two counterexamples, source environments and evidence limits.
prerequisites: Public access to primary papers/docs only.
No local GPU, profile, driver, process, build, test, or Strata result is required.
scopes.prerequisite_evidence: Public primary sources are available: the 2026 Data Path Fusion preprint (https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.10511v1), the VLDB GPU database characterization paper (https://www.vldb.org/pvldb/vol17/p441-cao.pdf), the Red Fox GPU relational-query paper (https://doi.org/10.1145/2544137.2544166), GPUQP (https://cse.hkust.edu.hk/catalac/papers/gpuqp_tods09.pdf), and the PVLDB relaxed-operator-fusion paper (https://www.vldb.org/pvldb/vol11/p1-menon.pdf). These sources suffice for a literature comparison without local measurements.

scopes.title: Tile-local attachment lifetime and external-memory traffic in tile-based rendering
scopes.finite_question: For tile-based deferred renderers, compare merged render passes/subpasses with tile-local attachment reuse, separate passes that store and reload intermediates, and transient/lazily allocated attachments with clear, discard, or resolve policies. How do attachment lifetime, dependencies, tile working-set capacity, sample count, later consumers, and framebuffer compression/decompression determine whether data stays on-chip or crosses external memory?
scopes.breadth_and_counterevidence: Use Khronos API guidance/specifications and primary vendor technical reports. Compare at least three pass/lifetime strategies in one table; distinguish API load/store/lifetime contracts from a driver choice to merge or retain data. Give a byte model for attachment stores/loads and MSAA resolve, labeled as arithmetic rather than measured bandwidth. Include counterexamples where external sampling, cross-frame persistence, dependencies, or tile capacity forces a store/reload or splits a pass. Treat lossless framebuffer compression only as a physical-traffic modifier, note decompression/access-pattern constraints, and do not survey codec algorithms. Record architecture/API revisions; do not transfer Mali/Apple behavior to Intel compute.
scopes.novelty_guard: No indexed report covers rasterization render-pass semantics or transient framebuffer lifetime. R835 is stencil time-skew/halo reuse; R839 is bank layout; R763/R769 are general compute residency/copy lifetime; R829 is lossless tensor compression. Focus only on tile-based graphics attachments, pass merging and load/store/discard/resolve; exclude stencil algorithms, generic compute fusion, bank conflicts, compression codecs, shader tiling, and Strata/Arc claims.
scopes.report_budget: 1,300–1,700 substantive words; at most 7 primary URLs; one attachment-lifetime/traffic table; counterexamples and explicit portability limits.
prerequisites: Public access to Khronos, Arm, Apple, and Microsoft source documentation and at least one technical report.
No graphics device, driver, profile, build, test, or local performance result is required.
scopes.prerequisite_evidence: Primary sources available include Vulkan TBR guidance (https://docs.vulkan.org/guide/latest/tile_based_rendering_best_practices.html), Arm Understanding Render Passes (https://documentation-service.arm.com/static/6560a5942c8b3557fee70a16), Arm GPU Best Practices issue 10 (https://documentation-service.arm.com/static/67a62b17091bfc3e0a947695), Apple TBDR docs (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metal/tailor-your-apps-for-apple-gpus-and-tile-based-deferred-rendering?language=objc), Microsoft D3D12 render passes (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/display/d3d12-render-passes), and Arm Bandwidth-Efficient Graphics (https://developer.arm.com/-/media/Files/pdf/graphics-and-multimedia/HPG-Bandwidth-Efficient-Graphics.pdf). These published artifacts need no local access.

scopes.title: Direction-optimized single-GPU BFS frontier representation and switching costs
scopes.finite_question: For single-GPU unweighted breadth-first search, compare top-down push over the active frontier, bottom-up pull over unvisited vertices with frontier-membership tests, and direction-optimized switching between them. How do frontier density, degree distribution, CSR/CSC or transpose availability, queue-versus-bitmap membership, duplicate discovery, and per-level conversion/compaction cost set the switch point?
scopes.breadth_and_counterevidence: Use original BFS/graph-processing papers and primary GPU framework papers. Compare three traversal strategies in one table; record graph family/scale, directed-edge convention, GPU, representation, preprocessing, frontier format, and whether throughput includes conversion/setup. Separate analytical edge-visit/storage estimates from measured TEPS. Include a sparse-frontier case where pull scans inactive vertices and dense-frontier/hub-heavy cases where top-down inspects many redundant edges but bottom-up may stop after finding one active neighbor; identify graph structures where switching does not pay. Treat duplicate-claim atomics only as a boundary condition, not an aggregation study. This is discovery/frontier direction, not sparse triangular dependency scheduling or destination reduction.
scopes.novelty_guard: Review/index metadata contains R786 graph destination fan-in/reduction, R854 SpTRSV dependency-ready scheduling, R778 sparse format conversion, R779 irregular gather/cache/TLB, and R759/R763 general work distribution, but no BFS push/pull frontier-switching study. Exclude multi-GPU partitioning, graph aggregation, SpTRSV counters/ready queues, SpMV/SpMM conversion, PageRank, generic scan/compaction algorithm surveys, and Strata implementation advice.
scopes.report_budget: 1,300–1,700 substantive words; at most 7 primary URLs; one frontier strategy/crossover table; graph/hardware measurement boundaries and counterevidence.
prerequisites: Public access to original graph-processing and GPU framework papers.
No local graph dataset, GPU, driver, profile, build, benchmark, or process state is required.
scopes.prerequisite_evidence: Public primary sources include Beamer et al., Direction-Optimizing BFS (https://doi.org/10.3233/SPR-130370); Merrill et al., Scalable GPU Graph Traversal (https://research.nvidia.com/sites/default/files/pubs/2012-02_Scalable-GPU-Graph/ppo213s-merrill.pdf); Gunrock (https://escholarship.org/uc/item/6xz7z9k0); GraphBLAST (https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.01407v1); and TurboBFS (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9007172/). The source set provides traversal alternatives without any local prerequisite.
